scope: P2 opt-in original-payment checkpoint custody and pinned read-only existing HTTP owner

selection.roadmap: P2 backend-bound persistent client/runner, preserving the original-payment recovery boundary
selection.rationale: The reviewed V5 payer retains the exact funding headers but no original funding body/context checkpoint. The existing pure checkpoint helper cannot reconstruct those absent original bytes. V6 atomically stores a caller-supplied checkpoint and reuses the existing owned HTTP lifecycle for pinned no-send reads.
selection.coverageLimit: This is a finite main/source and open-PR overlap selection, not a complete content review of every retained branch, a novelty claim from missing coverage, or a repeat of the stopped P0 composition selection.
selection.ownership: Self implementation followed by separate complete primary readback/review. No external worker or new helper/host was dispatched.

contract.enabledBy: Explicit V6 create/open factories only; no default or operational entry point opts in.
contract.binding: Exact stored transaction hash and funding HTTPS origin. paymentPayload is the exact PAYMENT-SIGNATURE canonical base64; paymentRequirements is the exact complete PAYMENT-REQUIRED canonical base64, not a recanonicalized selected requirement.
contract.callerPremises: The original requestId, contextId, request body and context are explicitly supplied original declared DATA. The store never infers them from a grant, funding status or another service request. Independent expected binding/digest pins must be retained outside this SQLite file and supplied on each read.
contract.retention: Funding pair and checkpoint share one existing BEGIN IMMEDIATE / COMMIT transaction. Repeated exact retention reads the existing revision/status/ambiguity and never replaces the checkpoint, clears uncertainty or resets consumed authority.
contract.versionBoundary: V1-V5 files are refused by V6; V5 refuses V6 before writable SQLite open. No adoption, schema migration, missing-record repair, deletion/reset or post-hoc checkpoint attachment API.
contract.resourceBoundary: The V6 root reuses the V5 HTTP child and original single resource slot/one-close path. Only a synchronous pinned DATA read is added; snapshots omit the checkpoint, raw store and funding credentials. Closed admission blocks reads.
contract.trustBoundary: Internal self-consistency checks are not authentication against a trusted local writer. A self-consistent rewritten context can be read only with matching changed pins; independently retained original pins reject it. No rollback resistance is established.

selectedNames: V6 atomically retains original payment and exposes pinned no-send reads across normal reopen
V5 remains explicit and V6 refuses V5 unchanged

launcher.reason: Reviewed native SQLite fchmod/fsync operations require the existing native execution premise; no OS or network sandbox is claimed.
launcher.timeoutMeaning: Not a hard lifetime, cancellation, native-cleanup or OS/network-sandbox guarantee.

execution.cleanup: HOLD_UNREGISTERED_SYNTHETIC_SQLITE_FILES; neither adopted for cleanup nor deleted. Native outcome and cleanup are separate.

independentReview.readOnlyGuardCorrections: The local readback callsite first had a Python conditional-spacing parse error, then expected a non-existent task status field. It was corrected to the actual state=CLOSED/outcome=SUCCESS schema. No additional task, native test, database mutation or original receipt rewrite was performed.
independentReview.codeConclusion: The new schema/factory flags are explicit. Existing V1-V5 schema decisions and preparation logic are preserved in source; only the selected V5 behavior below was executed. All current preparation/fence/status and owned-close writes remain on the existing owner/transaction paths.
assertions: Before-commit synthetic failure rolls back BOTH the pair and checkpoint; subsequent reads find neither.
Wrong funding hash/origin/payload/requirements and noncanonical checkpoint input are refused before retention.
Exact empty body, original opaque context spacing, both headers, binding and digests survive normal close/reopen.
An exact repeated retention at OUTCOME_UNKNOWN returns revision 3 with ambiguity latched; no authority reset.
The existing owned V6 HTTP facade reads only pinned DATA; the raw store and checkpoint are absent from snapshots.
One cached owned close blocks reads immediately and closes the native store exactly once.
Changed independent pins are refused without corrupting a valid store.
Self-consistent synthetic context rewriting fails the original independent pins; deleting the checkpoint refuses reopen without rewriting that file.
V5 preparation/idempotence and normal owned close still work; V6-on-V5 and V5-on-V6 refuse wrong versions without altering those selected files.
